correctness.rationale: The source payoffs exactly reduce to (1) for admissible rational/positive parameters. The invariant diagonal has a one-dimensional stable saddle branch with strict nullcline barriers and unique threshold for every interior x. The threshold spans x in (0,1), and scalar order plus no reverse crossing of the moving nullcline yields the basin trichotomy. Linearization yields both slopes/exponents; the positive slow eigencoordinate follows from the threshold barrier and the negative fast eigentangent, so the cusp coefficient cannot vanish. Smooth parameter dependence and a bounded Green integral yield the first-order response. The full-dimensional basin boxes follow from exact growth-sign inequalities, not numerical inference. A standalone program replays exact coefficients and 35,378 rational sign checks plus two numerical cross-checks.

value.rationale: The exact positive-volume defection-box construction demonstrates an important finite-grid limitation of the nine-point method used for a motivating game: a 100% observed sampled-cooperation score can coexist with an open defection basin. The entire symmetric-subspace basin graph is classified for an admissible two-parameter family, including exact nonlinear barriers, a noninteger vanishing-regulation cusp, and a first-order sensitivity integral. The endpoint behavior identifies genuine nonuniform dependence on initial regulatory uptake and supplies information beyond generic equilibrium existence or numerical basin sampling. It neither invents empirical policy claims nor extrapolates to reinforcement learners.
